subject: Deliverable gap & cost-econ runbook for MAP / eval plan
messages:
From: Katie Moore <katie@novamed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@novamed.com>

Subject: Deliverable gap & cost economics runbook — draft MAP items

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Alex and I pulled together an internal list of deliverables we expect in the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short evaluation plan for the pilot. We want to ensure we have the right cost assumptions baked into the MAP so procurement and our finance team won't block the pilot.

Quick background: our use case is a patient triage assistant with peak concurrent sessions estimated at ~1800/day and median session length ~220 tokens (in + out). We're sensitive to per-call latency (aim <400ms p95) and need a reliable estimate of tokens per dollar for budgeting.

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm the tokens/$ numbers you expect for the hosted pilot vs dedicated pool?
- Which caching and batching guardrails will you recommend for a live pilot (KV cache hit assumptions, hot-prefix prefetch)?
- Timeline: procurement needs a completed MAP + evaluation checklist and cost workbook by Nov 16 to meet our internal review on Nov 23. Can Redwood commit?

I've attached our draft MAP spreadsheet with the current deliverables column (NovaMed_MAP_cost_runbook_v0.xlsx). Please add a short "cost checks" tab describing the token model assumptions (tokenization profile, batching, cache hit rates) and any gating criteria you require.

Thanks — can we do a short sync tomorrow if possible?

—Katie
Katie Moore
Director of Product
NovaMed

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Katie Moore <katie@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deliverable gap & cost economics runbook — draft MAP items

Katie — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. We reviewed the draft MAP and added an initial "cost checks" worksheet (attached) that walks through our recommended assumptions and gating criteria. High-level summary below — I put the concrete numbers in token_econ_calcs.csv and the MAP workbook (NovaMed_MAP_cost_runbook_v0.xlsx).

Top-line assumptions (pilot hosted API, default small model series):
- Median tokens per session (round-trip) used for budget model: 220 tokens (you provided)
- Baseline tokens/$ (hosted, streaming enabled, no quantization): 0.0035 $/token (equivalent to ~285 tokens/$) — this is our conservative public-hosted estimate for initial forecasting.
- Dedicated pool guidance (reserved capacity, g4dn-like): expected effective tokens/$ = 0.00185 $/token (~540 tokens/$) after batching & sustained utilization (>=60% GPU fill).

Caching and batching guidance (impact on tokens/$):
- KV/prefix cache hit rate assumption: 12–20% on first-pass; with prompt engineering and session-level caching we commonly see 25–40% on repeat flows. We modeled three bands in the CSV (12%, 25%, 35%) to show sensitivity.
- Batching: p99 latency target <400ms constrains max request-aggregation window to ~25ms for this workload. With that window and expected concurrency, realistic average batch size = 3–7 tokens-per-inference step; at scale that gives ~1.6–2.3x throughput gain vs single-request baseline.
- Prefetch/hot-prefix: for triage we recommend a lightweight prefetch of top-3 intents per session (adds ~18 tokens of fixed cost but increases cache hits by ~8–12% in our pilot history).

Gating criteria for MAP acceptance (proposed):
1) Unit-econ smoke test: observed tokens/$ in pilot within 15% of modeled value at 2 different 2-hour windows (one peak, one off-peak).
2) Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end <400ms for 95% of traffic for 48 hours after canary.
3) Cache behavior: documented cache hit-rate >= modeled band for at least 24 hours of representative traffic.
4) Cost alerting: integration to NovaMed billing webhook or CSV export every 6 hours for cross-checking (we can provide the webhook template).

Proposed short evaluation plan & timeline (we updated eval_plan_v0.md attached):
- Nov 10: joint kickoff (30m) to walk the MAP and cost checks — propose 10:00am PT
- Nov 11–13: Redwood runs baseline smoke tests on hosted pilot image, shares token_econ_calcs.csv and a 24h sample export
- Nov 16: updated MAP + cost workbook delivered (you can use this for procurement)
- Nov 18–20: access granted to dedicated pool POC if required for a throughput check
- Nov 23: NovaMed internal review; target decision on purchase path

Immediate asks for us to hit Nov 16:
- You to confirm expected session concurrency shape (hourly profile or sample 24h histogram) — we used your 1800/day and assumed two peak hours with 20% of daily volume each.
- Any hard constraints from procurement on per-token ceiling (max acceptable $/token)

I'll join the kickoff tomorrow. If you prefer a different start time, let me know.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deliverable gap & cost economics runbook — draft MAP items

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 1:37 PM Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com> wrote:
> Caching and batching guidance (impact on tokens/$):
> - KV/prefix cache hit rate assumption: 12–20% on first-pass; with prompt engineering and session-level caching we commonly see 25–40% on repeat flows.
> - Batching: p99 latency target <400ms constrains max request-aggregation window to ~25ms for this workload. With that window and expected concurrency, realistic average batch size = 3–7 tokens-per-inference step; at scale that gives ~1.6–2.3x throughput gain vs single-request baseline.

Additional engineering clarifications from my side:
- The "batch size = 3–7" above is per-token-step (autoregressive): effectively that's how many requests we can merge for the same sequence length window. Operationally, for your profile (median 220 tokens/session) the economic benefit concentrates on shorter turns (where batching multiplies), so the CSV sensitivity includes a per-turn distribution assumption.
- KV cache hit math: we measure hits as % of continuation calls (not first-turn). If NovaMed's flows contain repeated clarifying prompts inside the same session, expect the higher end of the hit-rate band.
- Prefetch tradeoff: the +18 token fixed cost we suggested is conservative; for NovaMed you can tune to +8–12 tokens if intent candidates are narrower.

I'll run a quick micro-sim with the exact hourly shape if you send the 24h histogram (JSON or CSV). I noted the Nov 10 kickoff — I'll be on for the first 20m.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
